websearch.worst: A: Meta-analysis's substantial heterogeneity omitted while it is called 'the most rigorous source' (I2=74% for >1y weight; 97-98% earlier windows)
websearch.worst_summary_quote: This is the most rigorous source here, but the page is a clinic write-up of the abstract.
websearch.worst_page_quote: Although substantial heterogeneity was present, BS was associated with greater and sustained reductions in weight
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would take the 19.8 kg pooled long-term advantage as a firm estimate and would not know it rests on 4 RCTs plus 11 observational studies with high heterogeneity and no stated follow-up length.
websearch.notes: No journal page was fetchable (Wiley blocked); cedclinic write-up used as best available. Also omitted: NYU ASMBS 2025 figures (24% vs 5% at 2 years). Cleveland Clinic Nature Medicine figures (21.6% vs 6.8%, ~3,900 adults) and ASMBS 2024 review (25% at 10 years, ~50% regain) not in any usable page: maybe from an unfetched page. Pages compared: cedclinic, NBC Washington, NBC Boston, ReachMD; ASMBS, epocrates, pharmaceutical-journal pages under 2000 chars.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: How do long-term weight-loss outcomes of bariatric surgery compare with GLP-1 receptor agonists? Summarize the reported long-term (e.g., 2+ year or 5+ year) weight-loss figures for each, and note the study design, sample size, and follow-up duration if stated.
webfetch.notes: Numbers (MD, CIs, I2, 11,876/8,718 participants, 4 RCT + 11 observational, search date) all matched fetch.raw.txt. Primary source is a clinic write-up of Tahir et al. 2026, not the journal page (DOI 10.1111/dom.70676 returned no content).
